newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Airways to get $330 mln state aid.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Airways to get $330 mln state aid.

text.p: Kuwait will inject 100 million dinars ($330 million) into the state-owned Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) to help pay its debts and fund a planned restructuring, KAC chairman said in remarks published on Monday.

KAC and KIA has signed and agreement "according to which the latter (KIA) gives KAC 100 million dinars for restructuring and to contribute to debt payments," al-Rai al-Aam newspaper quoted Ahmad al-Meshari as telling a news conference for local media.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.
Meshari said KAC has settled $91 million of its total debt of $320 million, al-Watan newspaper said.
Kuwait plans to transform KAC into a shareholder company as a first step towards privatising the national flag carrier. Meshari said there was an inclination to privatise KAC in 1997.
KIA, the state investment arm, oversees Kuwait wide-ranging privatisation programme mobilised in 1994.

KAC has resorted to foreign and local borrowing to rebuiled its fleet following damages from the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation. About half of KAC's 21-aircraft fleet was destroyed during the occupation, said Meshari.
KAC's total assets are estimated at about 700 million dinars, said Meshrai.
KAC has two new Boeing Co 777s on order. It operates 15 Airbus Industries aircraft.
